re_line: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen · Albanese tells Putin to end the war 'now' · Unemployment jumps to 4.9pc · Fiji and Tonga declare drought emergencies · Politico: seven years' jail for photographing defence sites
morning_memo: Told Vladimir Putin to end the Ukraine war 'now' at APEC in Shenzhen, Anthony Albanese then stood in the same leaders' photograph as the Russian president, drawing criticism at home hours before Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held the first three-way summit of its kind.

Declared disaster and emergency status within days of each other, Fiji and Tonga are both in the grip of an El Nino-driven drought, while Vanuatu's internal affairs minister publicly rejected a parliamentary finding that 1,390 diplomatic passports are unaccounted for.

Jumped to 4.9 percent in October, Australia's unemployment rate hit a five-year high, undercutting the Reserve Bank's case for more tightening and handing Angus Taylor a fresh line on government spending.

top_stories.headline: Albanese tells Putin to end Ukraine war 'now' as Trump, Xi and Putin meet
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** called on Vladimir Putin to end his invasion of Ukraine "now" in an address to APEC leaders in Shenzhen, hours before Putin sat down with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping for the first trilateral meeting between the three powers. The leaders talked for about *90 minutes* at Kylin Villa, posing in front of their flags without shaking hands. Trump confirmed Ukraine was on the agenda alongside trade and nuclear arms control; the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty lapsed in February.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News (Stephen Dziedzic): "Leaders agree to Ukraine talks after Albanese urges Putin to end war 'now'" · also SMH

top_stories.headline: Unemployment hits 4.9 percent, the highest since 2021
top_stories.body: Australia's jobless rate rose 0.2 percentage points in October to *4.9 percent*, the highest since 2021, against market expectations of no change. Back-to-back monthly job losses undercut the Reserve Bank's argument that the labour market remains tight, and the three members who dissented from the last decision now look vindicated. The AFR reports bond traders pricing a small chance of a cut as soon as February. **Angus Taylor** blamed government "overspending".
top_stories.src_line: per SMH: "Unemployment hits five-year high as RBA squeezes jobs market" · also Bloomberg

top_stories.headline: Canberra to set seven-year prison term for photographing defence sites
top_stories.body: Australia will criminalise photographing designated defence sites with penalties of up to *seven years* in prison, Politico reports, as part of a broader expansion of defence powers that also covers immunity arrangements for United States troops in Australia. The package lands as American and British submarine activity at Australian bases grows under AUKUS.
top_stories.src_line: per Politico: "Australia to set 7-year prison term for photographing defense sites"

overnight_items.headline: Darwin Port rift deepens as Landbridge presses dispute action
overnight_items.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** said from Shenzhen the government remains determined to return the Port of Darwin to "Australian hands" before the next election, by acquisition or forced sale, and that negotiations continue. Landbridge, which holds the 99-year lease, disputes that characterisation and says it will press ahead with a formal dispute under the Australia-China Free Trade Agreement. The union covering port workers wants the matter settled.

overnight_items.headline: PNG says CHOGM leaders backed a Pacific Commonwealth office
overnight_items.body_text: Papua New Guinea's foreign minister **Justin Tkatchenko** said leaders at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in the Caribbean backed his proposal for a regional Commonwealth office in the Pacific, with the communique committing to "practical measures to support small island developing states participate meaningfully in international processes". Several of the 11 Pacific Commonwealth members, PNG included, have offered to host it. Tkatchenko said the organisation has been too focused on Africa and the Caribbean.

overnight_items.headline: Australian-run Nscale probes supply-chain ties to blacklisted Chinese firm
overnight_items.body_text: Nscale, the Australian-run data centre provider, has flagged potential supply-chain exposure to a blacklisted Chinese company, the AFR reports, amid renewed scrutiny of sensitive technology reaching China. The disclosure follows Canberra's decision this week to sign the United States-led San Francisco Declaration on protecting sensitive technology.

overnight_items.headline: Albanese defends joining the APEC family photo with Putin
overnight_items.body_text: The leaders of Australia and Canada defended standing in the APEC group portrait alongside Vladimir Putin as a courtesy to the host, China, the New York Times reports, after criticism at home. Deputy Prime Minister **Richard Marles** and Greens leader **David Shoebridge** traded positions on the photograph on Australian radio, with the AFR calling the image controversial.

overnight_items.headline: Teenager charged with terrorism offences over Parliament House hoax threats
overnight_items.body_text: A teenager accused of making hoax threats against Parliament House faces terrorism charges following an Australian Federal Police investigation. The charges follow a run of security incidents around federal facilities during the final sitting weeks of the parliamentary year.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji declares a state of disaster over El Nino drought
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji declared a national state of disaster as an El Nino-driven drought bites, with AFP reporting the government describing the dry spell as a crisis. Tourism officials are working with the National Disaster Risk Management Office to assess the effect on hotels, resorts and other tourism businesses.

pacific_wire.headline: Tonga declares a state of emergency as the drought worsens
pacific_wire.body_text: Tonga declared a state of emergency as the same El Nino drought deepens, RNZ reported, with the government classing the conditions a "natural hazard". Two Pacific states have now moved to emergency footing inside a week, with COP31 delegates from the region pressing donors on disaster finance.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu minister rejects finding that 1,390 diplomatic passports are missing
pacific_wire.body_text: Internal Affairs Minister **Andrew Solomon Napuat** rejected the public accounts committee's finding that *1,390* diplomatic passports are unaccounted for, saying every booklet printed between 2019 and 2025 is recorded and inviting auditors to inspect the stock. More than 1,000 were specimens sent to foreign border posts to help officers spot forgeries, he said, declining to name the countries. Vanuatu's citizenship by investment scheme has drawn foreign scrutiny of its travel documents.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu PM seeks US$160m for Pacific early warning systems
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu's prime minister called for *US$160 million* of investment to strengthen Pacific early warning systems and told COP31 that women are already driving climate action but must not carry the crisis alone. The same bulletin records the region presenting 70 renewable energy projects worth US$2.3 billion, and Papua New Guinea telling the conference it is matching ambition with action.

pacific_wire.headline: Marshall Islands minister: no departure from COP31 without a 1.5C overshoot response
pacific_wire.body_text: A Marshall Islands minister said the Pacific cannot leave COP31 without an answer on overshooting 1.5 degrees, as the Alliance of Small Island States pushed to convert the Belem Gender Action Plan into delivery. The bulletin also records Australia backing Pacific climate priorities, with **Chris Bowen** highlighting the clean energy shift.

pacific_wire.headline: Rabuka floats a standalone referendum before Fiji's general election
pacific_wire.body_text: Prime Minister **Sitiveni Rabuka** signalled Fiji could hold a standalone national referendum on constitutional reform before voters go to the polls at the general election, Islands Business reported. Constitutional amendment thresholds have been the central obstacle to the government's reform agenda.

pacific_wire.headline: Lawsuit seeks to halt the November 19 seabed lease sale off American Samoa
pacific_wire.body_text: Finafinau, a youth-centred environmental group in American Samoa, and the Natural Resources Defense Council sued the Trump administration to stop the auction of *31.5 million acres* of seabed off the territory for potential deep-sea mining. The plaintiffs argue the federal government rushed to open the ocean floor to commercial mining for the first time despite limited understanding of the consequences.

pacific_wire.headline: India pitches a four-pillar ocean and climate toolkit to the Blue Pacific
pacific_wire.body_text: New Delhi unveiled a four-pillar package of ocean and climate resilience measures for the Blue Pacific, seeking to turn diplomatic goodwill into delivery, Islands Business reported. India joins a crowded field of partners courting Forum members on climate finance and maritime capability.

pacific_wire.headline: Seven women elected in Niue, 35 percent of the Assembly
pacific_wire.body_text: Niue's May 2026 general election returned seven women to parliament, *35 percent* of the Assembly and the highest proportion in the country's history, according to a UNDP Samoa analysis carried by the Post-Courier. The piece tracks parallel efforts to lift youth participation in Niuean politics.

new_zealand.headline: Auckland mayor tells Chinese state television that Wellington is aligned with the US
new_zealand.body_text: Wayne Brown said in a full-length interview on Chinese state television that Wellington is aligned with the United States, RNZ reported, extending the fallout from his comments during a visit to China that democracy had "had its day". The interview follows criticism of the mayor's remarks from across the New Zealand political spectrum.

canberra_politics.headline: Burke rewrites the backpacker visa changes a second time
canberra_politics.body_text: Home Affairs Minister **Tony Burke** lifted the proposed cap on third-year working holiday visas, raised the number of days of regional work required for eligibility, and delayed the ballot until March, now rebranded a "ballot-style" Next Year Regional Work Guarantee, after pressure from agriculture, tourism and hospitality. Burke said a slower visa processing pace earlier this year gave him headroom and insisted the September commitment to cut net overseas migration still holds.

canberra_politics.headline: Coalition takes the primary vote lead in Morgan; Labor at an equal record low in YouGov
canberra_politics.body_text: Roy Morgan's federal poll has the Coalition ahead on primary vote, while a YouGov poll has Labor at an equal record low and the Greens at an equal record high, The Conversation reports. The readings follow Monday's Morgan result showing the Coalition leading on both primary and two-party preferred for the first time since the 2025 election.

canberra_politics.headline: Researcher says One Nation candidate's migrant welfare graph is 'completely wrong'
canberra_politics.body_text: **Peter Whiteford**, director of the Social Policy Institute at the Australian National University, told 702 ABC Sydney that a graph posted by One Nation's New South Wales upper house candidate **Katherine Deves** to argue for deep migration cuts was "very misleading" and its figures "completely wrong". Deves, a former Liberal candidate for Warringah, joined One Nation this year and was preselected on Sunday for the March state election.

canberra_politics.headline: Former Howard government minister Sharman Stone dies at 75
canberra_politics.body_text: Sharman Stone, a minister in the Howard government and member for the Victorian seat of Murray from 1996 for 20 years, died by voluntary assisted dying at 75 after an illness with glioblastoma. Her family said she "died on her own terms". Stone later served as Australia's ambassador for women and girls.

canberra_politics.headline: Politico: Australia's promised digital apprenticeships never materialised
canberra_politics.body_text: Politico has picked up the shortfall in the Commonwealth's digital traineeship program, after reporting this week that agencies hired 73 of a promised 1,000 digital trainees. The gap sits awkwardly against the government's push to lift public sector artificial intelligence capability.

business_economy.headline: Australian dollar set to shed its 2026 gain on rate-cut bets
business_economy.body_text: The Australian dollar is on course to surrender its gain for the year as traders price Reserve Bank cuts, Bloomberg reports. The currency traded at *0.6716* against the US dollar, down 1.34 percent, while the ASX 200 closed at 8,730, down 4.55 percent.

business_economy.headline: Housing body warns timber probe will lift build costs
business_economy.body_text: The Housing Industry Association warned that the Australian Trade Remedies Commission's dumping and subsidy investigation into Chinese structural timber could push up building costs, with timber the core structural element in about *80 percent* of Australian homes and roughly 20 percent of that timber imported. HIA industry policy chief **Simon Croft** said the association backs local manufacturing but the probe lands amid affordability and supply constraints. A finding is expected in April 2027.

business_economy.headline: AACo books record half-year operating profit of $64.8 million
business_economy.body_text: Australia's largest cattle company lifted half-year operating profit *63 percent* to a record $64.8 million, chief executive **David Harris** told shareholders, alongside the purchase of Adelong and investment in virtual fencing. Beef exports to China and north Asia remain central to the company's earnings.

business_economy.headline: RRJ-led consortium buys $619 million of an Australian coal miner's debt
business_economy.body_text: A consortium led by RRJ Capital has acquired *$619 million* of debt owed by an Australian coal miner, Bloomberg reports, as offshore capital moves into distressed thermal and metallurgical coal positions.

primary_documents.headline: Wong doorstop at Parliament House
primary_documents.body_text: The foreign minister held a doorstop at Parliament House during the final sitting fortnight, with transcripts also released of interviews on ABC News Breakfast and ABC Radio National.

primary_documents.headline: Trade minister announces the 2026 Australian Export Awards winners
primary_documents.body_text: The Minister for Trade and Tourism announced the 2026 Australian Export Awards winners, alongside a separate release on a record investment pipeline for Australian tourism.

calendar_watch.event: Final Australian parliamentary sitting week of 2026
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The government still needs to clear budget measures through the Senate before the parliamentary year ends.
Pacific delegations are pressing for an overshoot response and for early warning and renewable finance commitments.
One Nation is contesting the upper house on a migration-cut platform that is shaping the federal immigration debate.

calendar_watch.event: Start of the rebranded working holiday maker ballot-style scheme
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Determines whether Labor's net overseas migration reduction target survives contact with the agriculture and tourism sectors.

calendar_watch.event: Australian Trade Remedies Commission finding on Chinese structural timber
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Duties would raise input costs for roughly 20 percent of the timber used in Australian housing.

key_stat.label: Pacific renewable energy projects presented at COP31
key_stat.context: The region put 70 renewable projects on the table while Tuvalu sought a further US$160 million for early warning systems.

also_today.headline: Australia and the US should give ANZUS teeth and make it a deterrence network
also_today.body_text: Past the 75th anniversary of the ANZUS Treaty, with New Zealand's participation suspended since the mid-1980s over nuclear-free legislation, the authors argue sentimentality is colliding with the need to convert the treaty into a working deterrence network.

also_today.headline: Washington built the hub-and-spokes, Australia and Japan are rewiring it
also_today.body_text: A decade of alliance-building has given middle powers a security architecture that no longer runs through one capital, the Interpreter argues, as Canberra and Tokyo thicken bilateral and minilateral ties.

also_today.headline: Locally led climate finance needs apprenticeships, not more readiness workshops
also_today.body_text: **Jale Samuwai**, who manages the Climate Finance Access Network for the Pacific, and a co-author argue Pacific climate finance fails at the last mile because of brittle bookkeeping rather than a lack of funds, and that mentoring builds durable capability where workshops do not.

also_today.headline: Speers: Trump creates chaos, Australia keeps moving closer
also_today.body_text: David Speers writes that despite the awkwardness of the Shenzhen trilateral, Australia tightened its alignment with Washington this week by signing the 10-nation San Francisco Declaration on sensitive technology and joining the first Quad leaders' meeting in two years, in Manila.

also_today.headline: Canada to sign a major JORN deal
also_today.body_text: Canada is set to sign a major agreement on the Jindalee Operational Radar Network, Australian Defence Magazine reports, extending Australian over-the-horizon radar technology to a second Five Eyes partner.

also_today.headline: Report says data centre pollution could rival coal power stations
also_today.body_text: Emissions from Australia's data centre rollout could rival those of coal-fired power stations, according to a report carried by the ABC, as calls grow for a moratorium on new centres.

opeds_today.headline: The unusual people you meet when you go to China
opeds_today.central_argument: Australians engaging in China should expect interlocutors who are more complex than official framing suggests.
opeds_today.summary: Written in the week Anthony Albanese met Xi Jinping and other officials in China, the piece recounts encounters with Chinese interlocutors and argues against flattening them into a single official type. It touches on influence operations and espionage risk alongside genuine engagement.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Bears on how Australian officials and researchers calibrate engagement risk during a period of renewed leader-level contact.

opeds_today.headline: Trump's AI push has Albanese's signature, but another country is quickly gaining ground
opeds_today.central_argument: Australia has signed on to the US artificial intelligence agenda, but a competitor is closing the gap.
opeds_today.summary: The United States Studies Centre examines Canberra's decision to join the US-led artificial intelligence declaration and what it means for Australia's technology alignment.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Frames the trade-offs in Australia's technology alignment as Canberra signs successive US-led digital agreements.

opeds_today.headline: Fighting fires, sparking curiosity
opeds_today.central_argument: Australia's fire-fighting deployment to East Kalimantan could broaden public interest in Indonesia.
opeds_today.summary: The Interpreter argues the mission in East Kalimantan is a rare, visible piece of Australian cooperation with Indonesia that could build wider domestic familiarity with the relationship.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Relevant to how Canberra builds public constituency for its most consequential neighbourhood relationship.
